description: Observable Framework layer: overview page demonstrating a JavaScript data loader and Plot chart.

buildHints.whenToUse: Interactive data dashboards, analytics UIs, internal reporting tools, or any project where markdown-first reactive notebooks are the primary surface.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Observable Framework serves on port 3000 with HMR; the home page renders immediately.
Pages live in `src/` as `.md` files — `src/index.md` is the home page, `src/overview.md` is the demo Overview page.
Data loaders live in `src/data/` — `src/data/rows.json.ts` runs at build time and its JSON output is consumed in `overview.md` via `FileAttachment`.
Run `pnpm build` to emit a fully-static site to `dist/` — no server runtime in production, deploy to any CDN.
gotchas: `Plot` and `Inputs` are Observable Framework globals in `.md` pages — do NOT import them; adding an explicit import will cause a runtime error.
Data loaders run at build time (and dev-server boot), not in the browser — they have full Node.js access but must write JSON, CSV, or plain text to stdout.
The `observablehq.config.ts` `pages` array controls sidebar navigation — add a new entry whenever you add a new `.md` file in `src/`.
TypeScript in `.md` fenced code blocks is not typechecked by `tsc` — only `observablehq.config.ts` and explicit `src/**/*.ts` files are covered.
architectureNotes: Each `.md` page is an isolated reactive notebook — JavaScript cells run top-to-bottom and can reference earlier cells by name.
Data loaders decouple heavy computation from the browser — run SQL, Node scripts, or any subprocess as a loader and ship only the serialised output.
